header.app: Example Meal Planner (iOS and Android), an invented meal planning app
sources_read: App Store Connect exports (sources; territories for search and browse)
Play Console exports (traffic sources; countries for search)
Google Ads, Meta, TikTok and Snapchat through the InsightfulPipe MCP
Apple Ads and AppLovin exports from the user
App Store and Google Play listings for the app and 3 rivals in the United States and Germany
header.z_test_note: The z test treats unique-device counts as independent trials, so it is an approximation.

answer: App Store: mix shift only. Blended conversion fell from 10.01% to 8.19% while downloads rose from 33,870 to 37,600. Browse impressions grew from 58,000 to 181,000 during the Today feature and browse converts at 3.0%; no source's rate really dropped. Google Play: real drop on Google Play search, 28.67% to 26.15% blended.
Sure organic: 65.2% of App Store downloads and 78.9% of Play acquisitions.
Top fix: test the old Play icon and screenshots against the new ones, about 4,720 acquisitions at stake this period.

rate_definitions.google_play: store listing acquisitions / store listing visitors

listing_changes_compared.change: Apple featured the app in a Today tab story from 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-15 (not a change we made)
listing_changes_compared.reading: Explains the mix shift: browse impressions tripled at a low browse rate. The listing did not get worse.

listing_changes_compared.change: New icon and a new screenshot set went live on the default store listing
listing_changes_compared.reading: The search drop starts with it. A lead, not proof: test it (fix 1).
No source changed at that date in a way the data can separate.

network_claims.network: Google Ads (App campaigns, Apple App Store)

apple_ads_search_results.source: Apple Ads export from the user

apple_ads_other_placements.source: Apple Ads export from the user
apple_ads_other_placements.note: Today tab and Search tab installs: listed apart and not subtracted, because Apple does not say which bucket they land in

app_store.flag: 5,990 referrer downloads are not claimed by any network: organic links, untracked campaigns, or paid installs the networks missed. Reported apart, never as organic.

network_claims.source: export from the user (no MCP connector for it)

google_play.flag: Networks claim 12,700 Android installs, 1,800 more than the 10,900 acquisitions Play recorded under Ads and referrals. Not subtracted below zero: Meta counts view-through installs by default, Google Ads counts by its own conversion settings, and Play counts a user once across devices and leaves out reinstalls. A full reconciliation with a measurement partner is a separate job.

paid_vs_organic.note: Fixes are judged on organic sources first; paid traffic lands on the page each campaign points to.

gaps.rule: gap when z <= -2 and the segment base is at least 1,000; 'All other' rows are not a segment and are left out

reasons.segment: Germany, App Store search and Google Play search
reasons.reason: Rivals show German listings in Germany; this app shows English text. Fits a localization gap; price level and brand awareness could also play a part.

near_misses.reading: Below the rest, but the z test calls it noise; not a gap.

fixes_ranked.fix: Test the old icon and screenshot set against the new ones on the default Play listing
fixes_ranked.evidence: Search conversion fell from 32.0% to 28.0% on 118,000 visitors (z = -21.29, real). It starts with the icon and screenshot change on 2026-10-06; explore and ads and referrals held steady. A lead, not proof.
fixes_ranked.the_job: Run a store listing experiment: old icon and screenshots against the new set, on Google Play search traffic. Roll back only if the old set wins.

fixes_ranked.fix: Publish a German store listing on Google Play
fixes_ranked.evidence: Germany converts 19.0% on 14,000 search visitors against 29.2% for the rest of Play search (z = -25.26). All 3 rivals show a German title and short description in Germany; this app shows its English listing.
fixes_ranked.listing_element: local-language listing (title, short description, screenshot captions)
fixes_ranked.the_job: Translate the title, short description and screenshot captions into German, then test it with a store listing experiment for German users.

fixes_ranked.fix: Localize the App Store product page for Germany
fixes_ranked.evidence: Germany converts 5.0% on 30,000 search impressions against 9.7% for the rest of App Store search (z = -26.48). All 3 rivals have a German title and description in the German storefront; this app's is the English text.
fixes_ranked.the_job: Add a German localization in App Store Connect (name, subtitle, keywords, screenshots), then compare German search conversion over the next 28 days.

fixes_note: Installs at stake are estimates for the current 28 days, assuming the segment reaches the comparison rate. Don't add rows up: German Play search visitors sit in both fix 1 and fix 2.

worth_testing.difference: Rivals B and C show a preview video; this app has none.
worth_testing.why_not_a_fix: No measured gap points to it: explore and ads and referrals held steady, and the search drop lines up with the icon and screenshot change, not the video.
worth_testing.test: A store listing experiment with a preview video, after the icon test ends.

worth_testing.difference: Rival A has 10 screenshots in the United States storefront; this app has 8.
worth_testing.why_not_a_fix: App Store search in the United States converts above the rest of the store, so no gap points to it.
worth_testing.test: A Product Page Optimization treatment with two more screenshots.

not_checked: Device split (iPhone and iPad, Android phone and tablet): not in the exports.
Country gaps cover the current period only: the previous period's territory split was not exported.
Apple Ads installs from the Today tab and Search tab (300) are listed but not placed in any bucket.
App Store preview videos: the connector does not return them and the user did not say, so they are not compared.
No measurement partner data: network totals are compared with the stores only.
